title: Refactor monolithic FastAPI app into APIRouter modules (users, posts, comments)
description: A FastAPI app with users, posts, and comments all in src/app.py must be split into separate APIRouter modules without breaking any tests.

task_spec.prompt:
The FastAPI app in src/app.py has three domains (users, posts, comments) all defined in one file. Refactor into a modular layout WITHOUT changing any HTTP routes or response shapes:

1. Create src/routes/__init__.py (empty).
2. Create src/routes/users.py — move all user-related state (_users, _next_user_id) and the three user endpoints into a users_router = APIRouter(prefix='/users', tags=['users']). The router must export a reset_users() function.
3. Create src/routes/posts.py — move posts state + endpoints into posts_router = APIRouter(prefix='/posts', tags=['posts']). Export reset_posts().
4. Create src/routes/comments.py — move comment state + create_comment + list_comments into comments_router = APIRouter(tags=['comments']). Keep the path /posts/{post_id}/comments. Export reset_comments(). Comments must still validate that the post exists — they should import posts_router state or a shared getter.
5. Rewrite src/app.py to only: import and include the three routers, define app = FastAPI(), and define reset() that calls reset_users() + reset_posts() + reset_comments().
6. All 7 existing tests must pass without modification. Run uv run pytest tests/ -q to confirm.
7. Run uv run ruff check src/ to confirm no lint errors.
required_artifacts: src/app.py reduced to router includes + reset()
uv run ruff check src/ clean
success_criteria: No routes changed — identical HTTP surface
State properly encapsulated in each module
Cross-module dependency (comments checking post existence) handled cleanly
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
